facts: Acceleration $=\dfrac{\text{change in speed}}{\text{change in time}}$, found from the gradient of a speed-time graph, in m/s².
A line sloping **up** shows the object speeding up (accelerating); a line sloping **down** shows it slowing down (**decelerating**).
A **horizontal** segment shows a constant speed — the gradient is $0$, so the acceleration is $0$.

Compare gradients using the axis scales: a greater gradient magnitude means a greater acceleration or deceleration magnitude. A visually steeper line on a differently scaled graph need not represent a greater rate.
steps: Identify the stage of the journey the question asks about, and read the speed at its start and end.
Find the change in speed and the time taken for that stage.
Divide to find the acceleration (or deceleration), in m/s².

workedExamples.solution_text:
Acceleration is the gradient: change in speed divided by the time taken for that stage.

From $0$ to $4$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{16-0}{4-0}\\&=4\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

From $4$ to $10$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{16-16}{10-4}\\&=0\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
The graph is horizontal: the car travels at a constant speed of $16$ m/s.

From $10$ to $14$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{0-16}{14-10}\\&=-4\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
The deceleration magnitude is $4$ m/s².

From $14$ to $18$ s, the speed stays at $0$, so the car is stationary and its acceleration is $0$ m/s².

From $18$ to $24$ s:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Acceleration}&=\frac{12-0}{24-18}\\&=2\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$
Use the $6$ seconds after departure; exclude the time spent stationary.

Vehicle A:

$\begin{aligned}\text{Initial acceleration}&=\frac{24-0}{4-0}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Final deceleration magnitude}&=\frac{24-0}{16-12}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

Vehicle B:

$\begin{aligned}\text{Initial acceleration}&=\frac{12-0}{6-0}\\&=2\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\text{Final deceleration magnitude}&=\frac{12-0}{14-12}\\&=6\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$

Vehicle A accelerates faster. Both vehicles have the same deceleration magnitude: $6$ m/s².

foundation.solution_text:
Between $5$ and $12$ seconds the graph is horizontal, so the speed is not changing.
Acceleration $=\dfrac{\text{change in speed}}{\text{change in time}}=\dfrac{0}{7}=0$, so an unchanging speed means an acceleration of $0$ m/s².

Car X: acceleration $=\dfrac{18}{6}=3$ m/s²
Car Y: acceleration $=\dfrac{12}{6}=2$ m/s²

Train P: deceleration $=\dfrac{20}{10}=2$ m/s²
Train Q: deceleration $=\dfrac{20}{4}=5$ m/s²

While waiting at the station (from $14$ to $18$ seconds) the speed stays at $0$, so that stage cannot be used for the departure's acceleration.
From $18$ s ($0$ m/s) to $22$ s ($16$ m/s):
Acceleration $=\dfrac{16-0}{22-18}$
$=\dfrac{16}{4}$
$=4$ m/s²
